transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Time: 15:00 - 15:57 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Morgan (Seastone Head Eng), Samir N. (Seastone Sec), Priya R. (PM), Evan H. (DevOps)

Summary: Quick kickoff to align on onboarding/runway for Seastone Logistics' pilot. Primary topics: security artifacts (SOC2/ISO), network topology for Private deployment (VPC/Peering/k8s), tenant mapping for multi-tenant routing, latency vs cost constraints, and next steps for a two-week pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick round of intros and then walk the activation plan, should be under an hour so appreciate that
[00:18] Leah (Seastone): hi this is leah, i'm head of eng, i'll own the project internally, Samir is our sec lead, Priya is PM and Evan will run staging
[00:28] Maya: perfect thanks. Jordan do you want to run the high-level runbook?
[00:33] Jordan (Redwood SE): sure, i'll keep it high level then dive where needed. goal is pilot: 2 weeks, validate latency under 220ms p95 for our inference calls, and verify data residency + KMS integration. we'll propose hosted first then show dedicated/private options if needed
[00:52] Samir: quick flag, we have corporate policy: keys must be in our HSM, no long-term logs stored outside our account, and SAML/SSO is required for team access. also need audit log retention 12 months
[01:12] Jordan: understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem key wraps — there is a handoff for providing key access. we'll document the exact KMS flow in the security runbook
[01:30] Evan: how intrusive is the private deploy? we run k8s in a prod and a staging cluster; we want minimal network peering and maybe a sidecar approach
[01:42] Jordan: you can either do VPC peering with a private endpoint or our on-prem agent can run as a container - most customers pick VPC peering for predictable latency; note peering requires CIDR allowances and routing updates
[02:02] Priya: timeline wise we want pilot in January, but if we can do a staging validation earlier that'd be ideal. what's realistic?
[02:12] Maya: if we get SOC docs and staging access this week, Jordan can run a pre-check and we could aim for a Dec/Jan pilot start. i'll put proposed dates in the follow-up
[02:28] Leah: can you also send a simple tenant mapping template? we have multiple business units, need to route requests to different model variants
[02:37] Jordan: yes — we'll share a CSV template. note that routing by tenant can be done via per-tenant API keys or via header-based routing; there are tradeoffs for caching and KV cache reuse
[02:55] Samir: what's KV cache again? we've seen it in docs, is that safe to share across tenants?
[03:04] Jordan: good q — KV cache is per-request prefix caching, generally we keep caches isolated per-tenant to avoid cross-tenant leakage; for shared models we can do namespace separation. i'll add this to security notes (apologies if the doc earlier said K-V cash in one place ha)
[03:26] Maya: quick poll — are you leaning hosted API or dedicated capacity for the pilot?
[03:33] Leah: hosted to start, but if latency or cost is off we'll look at dedicated. Samir prefers dedicated for isolation reasons
[03:42] Samir: yes, dedicated is easier for meeting our internal audit but comes with a commit and different pricing, so we want to see numbers
[03:50] Jordan: we can run small benchmarks in staging to show p95 and cost per 1k tokens across profiles (int8 quantized vs fp16). i'll prepare that and share a benchmark sheet
[04:05] Evan: about quantization — any gotchas for us running on our instance types? we use AWS g5a and some g4s for dev; we want recommended profiles
[04:17] Jordan: we'll propose quant profiles per instance family; some models are better with q4_0 or q5_1 — we'll list recommendations. also, sequence length affects kernel selection so share typical token lengths
[04:33] Priya: success metrics: user-facing latency p95 under 250ms, cost below $X per 1k tokens (we'll fill X in), and no PII stored outside our account. Priya to confirm exact cost ceiling
[04:47] Priya: yes i'll confirm in the doc by tomorrow, but that's the rough constraints
[05:00] Maya: great, we also noted stakeholders: Leah running exec comms, Samir security, Evan infra, Priya PM — i'll annotate the onboarding plan with RACI
[05:12] Leah: about logs and debug traces — we need trace redaction and token-level cost breakdowns but Samir wants minimal sensitive payload retained
[05:24] Jordan: Redwood Console lets you toggle log retention and redaction. default for private is no log retention outside your account; for hosted we can enable shorter retention windows and PII redaction rules
[05:38] Samir: can you share an example of the audit log schema? we need to map to our SIEM
[05:45] Maya: yes that's part of the security packet i'll send, includes fields and sample events
[05:51] [08:10] Maya: (screen share) here's the onboarding runbook: step 1 access, step 2 network, step 3 model onboarding, step 4 monitoring and run SLA checks
[08:32] Jordan: head's up on model onboarding — version pinning is recommended; we can do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller variants if a rollout fails
[08:46] Leah: can we do A/B across regions? we have users in NA and EU and need local inference for latency and data residency
[08:56] Jordan: yes, multi-region routing is supported, and you can pin EU data to EU-hosted instances. for private customers we can provision in their region or do dedicated in a nearby region
[09:14] Evan: about networking again — NAT gateways and outbound egress rules? we need to limit outbound to our SIEM and Redwood endpoints only
[09:25] Jordan: recommended outbound list will be provided; for private you can also run through our peered setup with no public egress if desired
[09:36] [15:02] Priya: question on cost model — hosted is usage-based, dedicated is commit-based; do you have guidance on when to switch?
[15:12] Maya: generally after predictable sustained throughput for 2-3 months, dedicated is recommended. we'll include an estimate based on your projected Q1 traffic in the follow-up pricing sheet
[15:24] Samir: security review sequence — can we do an initial attestation review, followed by a technical deep dive, then an on-site audit if needed?
[15:33] Jordan: that's the usual flow. we can do the technical deep dive remotely; on-site is rare but possible for Private/on-prem packages
[15:40] Leah: any limitations on model size or KV cache for long context? we anticipate ~8k tokens typical hits occasionally 25k
[15:50] Jordan: some models and infra are optimized up to certain seq lengths; very long contexts require specific kernel choices — we'll list supported sequence strategies and recommend episodic truncation vs streaming
[16:10] Maya: ok wrapping to next steps — i'll send security packet, Jordan will schedule the deep-dive, Evan will share staging access, and Priya will confirm KPIs
[16:21] Leah: sounds good. Samir anything else on sec?
[16:26] Samir: just want the encryption flow and verification steps documented; also confirm the audit log retention & export process
[16:33] Jordan: yes we'll add a short appendix for audit exporting to S3 or your SIEM with schema mapping
[16:41] [25:00] Maya: final quick Qs — do you have an internal approver timeline for procurement?
[25:08] Leah: procurement has a 3-week review once we give scope+SLA; legal loop may add time but we'll aim to align procurement and security reviews in parallel
[25:20] Maya: ok we'll factor that in for the pilot start date proposal
[25:26] Evan: one last infra detail — can we test a small synthetic workload to validate p95 before we load prod traffic?
[25:33] Jordan: yes we have a benchmark harness we can run in your staging; it'll produce p50/p95/cost per 1k tokens across profiles
[25:45] Priya: let's schedule the benchmark run in next two weeks if possible
[25:51] Jordan: will do, aiming for next Tue/Thu windows, i'll follow up with calendar invites
[26:02] Maya: recap of owners and dates — Maya send security docs by 11/30, Jordan technical deep-dive on 12/02, Evan staging access by 11/29, Priya confirm KPIs by 11/28
[26:18] Leah: thanks all, appreciate the clarity, excited to get started

Closing:
[56:30] Maya: thanks everyone for the time. i'll follow up with the packet and invites. we'll leave the deep technical items for the Jordan session next week. bye
[56:40] Jordan: thanks, bye
